prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He was selected for the post (1) / because of he was familiar (2) / with both urban as well as rural way of life. (3) / no error (4)
options: He was selected for the post
with both urban as well as rural way of life.
explanation: 'Both' is correlated with 'and', never with 'as well as': 'with both urban and rural ways of life'. (The 'of' in 'because of he was' is also superfluous.)

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: It is not easy for an actor (a) / to earn respect from both, the fans (b) / as well as the critics, (c) / no error (d)
options: It is not easy for an actor
to earn respect from both, the fans
explanation: 'Both' must be followed by 'and', and the comma after it is wrong: 'to earn respect from both the fans and the critics'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Between you and I, (1) / I am convinced (2) / that this painting by Neetu shows greater artistry than that of Reshma. (3) / No Error (4)
options: that this painting by Neetu shows greater artistry than that of Reshma.
explanation: 'Between' is a preposition and needs object pronouns, so 'Between you and I' should be 'Between you and me'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Scientists show that there is a curious (1) / relationship among a lion's life span and (2) / the pattern of spots on each side of its face. (3) / No error (4)
options: Scientists show that there is a curious
relationship among a lion's life span and
the pattern of spots on each side of its face.
explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two things; with two items (life span and spot pattern) use 'relationship between a lion's life span and'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: There was a (a) / comparison between (b) / you and he (c) / no error (d)
explanation: After the preposition 'between', the pronoun must be in the objective case: 'you and him'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: They had tried (a) / to win deceptively (b) / and this resulted in both failing or destroying others, (c) / No error (d)
options: and this resulted in both failing or destroying others,
explanation: 'Both' pairs with 'and', not 'or': 'resulted in both failing and destroying others'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Both Renu as well as (a)/ her sister are very tall (b)/ and are in the basketball team, (c)/ No Error (d)
options: and are in the basketball team,
explanation: 'Both ... as well as' is incorrect; the correlative is 'both ... and', so write 'Both Renu and her sister'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: After the examination is over, (1)/ you must hand over (2)/ both the answer booklets as well as the question paper (3)/ to the invigilator. (4)
options: both the answer booklets as well as the question paper
explanation: 'Both' must be followed by 'and': 'both the answer booklets and the question paper'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: When it was time to (a)/ chose between staying or leaving the country (b)/, she choose to stay back. (c)/ no error (d)
options: chose between staying or leaving the country
explanation: After 'to' the base form 'choose' is needed, and 'between' takes 'and': 'to choose between staying and leaving the country'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: Both the operations manager (A) / as well as the head of quality assurance (B) / were summoned to present the compliance report. (C) / No Error (D)
options: as well as the head of quality assurance
were summoned to present the compliance report.
explanation: 'Both' must be paired with 'and', not 'as well as'; correct it to 'Both the operations manager and the head of quality assurance'.

prompt: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
sentence: Both Reeta and Ronika / has won / the dance competition / this year.
explanation: 'Both ... and' joins two subjects to form a plural subject, so the verb must be 'have won'.

prompt: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case
sentence: no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. These shoes are cheap as well durable.
explanation: 'as well' cannot join two adjectives here; the correlative pair 'both ... and' correctly links 'cheap' and 'durable'.
